versions.changelog: Estrella TV (KETD) streams again from its new live page (17 stations enabled; use "Load this market's stations and teams" to pick it up). A station with nothing to play right now, such as one that streams only during its newscasts, shows a "Nothing is streaming right now" screen instead of a playback error. Test now names a bot check when a site shows one. Team schedules that fail to load (after a restart, say) are retried within minutes instead of half an hour.

Coverage area: set a maximum distance and your location (or use this device's location) to keep only nearby stations in Live TV; each station's city and distance show in the settings. Stations set up by an earlier version get their locations automatically. KWGN CW2, KDVR FOX31 and KXRM FOX21 stream again (16 stations enabled); use "Load this market's stations and teams" to turn them on.

Channels added or removed while Jellyfin was down (for example by upgrading the plugin) now show up in Live TV on their own: the first sync after a restart refreshes the guide when the station list changed, instead of waiting for Sync now or the daily guide refresh.

Wider coverage: the Denver market now reaches every TV market covering part of Colorado plus Cheyenne (30 stations, 13 enabled, up from 6), including Gray Television stations such as KKTV 11, whose streams now play (also behind DNS ad blockers). Local games prefer Denver stations. Use "Load this market's stations and teams" in the settings to get the new stations.

Bug fixes: streams no longer stall at each refresh, a failed Test leaves a playing channel alone, sturdier settings page (clear errors for a wrong sidecar URL or API key), Local Sports guide starts with the pre-game, and better stream detection on station pages.

name: Local Broadcast
overview: Local TV stations' free web streams in Live TV, local sports first
description: Adds your market's local TV stations to Live TV as an M3U tuner with a guide, using the free live streams on the stations' own websites (found by the local-broadcast sidecar, a small Docker container). Stations airing a local team's game come first, and a Local Sports channel always plays the station that has the game.
